met_analysis:
The Low Pressure Area over southwest Madhya Pradesh and adjoining north Vidarbha lies over Southwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 13th September 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extending upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is likely to move west-northwestwards across southeast Rajasthan & adjoining north Gujarat during next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Disha, centre of Low Pressure Area over Southwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood Betul, Brahmpuri, Jagdalpur, Kalingapatnam and thence east- southeastwards to Westcentral Bay of Bengal.
The trough now runs from Eastcentral Arabian Sea to Gangetic West Bengal across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, north Chhattisgarh & Jharkhand and extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & neighbourhood between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies south Tamil Nadu coast & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan adjoining Eastcentral Arabian sea persists and now seen at 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 73°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists.
The trough from Southwest Arabian Sea to centre of Low Pressure Area over West Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood across Eastcentral Arabian Sea, Konkan & Goa, Madhya Maharashtra at 5.8 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from cyclonic circulation associated with Low Pressure Area over West Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood to Gulf of Mannar across Marathwada, North Interior Karnataka, Rayalaseema & Tamil Nadu extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central Assam & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
